summary.headline: Canara Bank Q4 FY26: FY26 net profit up 12.69% to Rs 19,187 crore; Q4 operating profit hit by one-time base effect and MTM losses, with ECL impact of about Rs 10,000 crore flagged.
summary.overview: Management reported global business of Rs 28.0 lakh crore (up 12.11%), global advances up 15.30% to Rs 12.37 lakh crore, and FY26 net profit of Rs 19,187 crore (up 12.69%). Quarterly profitability fell versus Q3 because Q3 included Rs 1,930 crore of one-time listing gains from Canara HSBC and Canara Robeco stake dilution, plus about Rs 800 crore of MTM losses in Q4 from a rise in bond yields. Asset quality improved on a YoY basis: GNPA 1.84% (down 110 bps), net NPA 0.43%, PCR 94.21%, credit cost 0.59%. Management guided NIM at 2.5-2.6% and advances growth at 11-12%, and said ECL transition (about Rs 10,000 crore, staggered over four years) can be absorbed from profits.

segments.name: RAM (retail, agri, MSME)
segments.commentary: RAM credit grew 19.73% to Rs 7.30 lakh crore; RAM share of loan book is 59% versus a target of 60:40 RAM-to-corporate mix.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail credit grew 32.93% to Rs 2.96 lakh crore; housing up 17.55% to Rs 1.24 lakh crore; vehicle loans up 26.33% to Rs 26,070 crore.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book Rs 2.45 lakh crore (about 20% of advances): agri Rs 1.54 lakh crore, non-agri Rs 91,000 crore. Agri gold growing about 15% and total gold loans 33-34%, per management.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME credit grew 12.85% to Rs 1.57 lakh crore; MSME accounted for Rs 1,333 crore of Q4 slippages.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate is about 41% of loan book; sanctioned-but-not-disbursed pipeline about Rs 20,000 crore and undisbursed corporate about Rs 20,000 crore.

guidance_outlook: Advances growth guidance of 11-12% for FY27; management said it expects to exceed this, as FY26 guidance of 10-11% was beaten at 15.30%.
NIM expected to hover at 2.5-2.6%, supported by a 9 bps QoQ improvement in Q4 and repricing of bulk deposits.
ROA guided above 1%; management said the bank can sustain it after ECL transition.

ECL: estimated additional provision about Rs 10,000 crore (Rs 2,500 crore stage 2 floor move from 0.4% to 5%, Rs 2,500-5,000 crore PD-related, Rs 2,500 crore non-fund); can be staggered over four years; system-level implementation in September 2026 with E&Y as knowledge partner; impact on CRAR about 1%.
Management expects the MTM loss of about Rs 800 crore not to recur in Q1 FY27; Rs 300 crore big-ticket recovery already received in Q1 FY27.
Dividend Rs 4.20 per share proposed. Capital raise possible if needed; board approval pending, with details expected within a couple of months.
PSLC income expected around Rs 2,500-3,000 crore in FY27, similar to FY26 (analyst figures of 6,500 crore were not clearly confirmed).
capex_capacity: Capital: CRAR 17.04%; management said the ECL impact would reduce CRAR by about 1% if absorbed upfront.
Digital: 1,204 crore digital transactions in FY26 versus 940 crore prior year; mobile app ranked number one on Google Play.
Network: 3,000 customer relationship managers working on cross-sell to families.
Subsidiaries: stake sold in Canara HSBC Life (14.5%) and Canara Robeco AMC (13%); management said no further dilution is planned.
demand_pricing: Credit demand strong; RAM growth led advances, and management said it avoids low-yield advances and is pricing bulk deposits more carefully.
Yield on advances fell only 5 bps QoQ despite a 25 bps repo cut in December because about 50% of the portfolio is repo-linked.
Deposit repricing: retail term deposits were raised in Dec-Jan by about 30-35 bps; management said this shifted flows from bulk to retail, lowering cost of deposits.
Gold loan interest rates not increased; LTV kept below 70%.
Agri and MSME share of the loan book has declined over the last four quarters, per management's confirmation of the analyst's question.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating and net profit fall QoQ, and what drove the lower NIM and treasury income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q3 had Rs 1,930 crore of one-time listing gains, which did not recur. Q4 had about Rs 800 crore of MTM losses from bond yields moving from 6.59% to 7.05%. TWO recovery was 6,500 crore in FY26 versus 6,800 crore in FY25, with quarterly swings from large-ticket resolutions.

qa_highlights.question: How much ECL provision is needed and how will it be met?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated about Rs 10,000 crore total impact (Rs 2,500 crore stage 2 floor move, Rs 2,500-5,000 crore PD-related, Rs 2,500 crore non-fund). It can be staggered over four years, and profit of Rs 19,000-20,000 crore allows absorption upfront. Absolute stage-wise provisions will be shared after system implementation. Standard provision is Rs 4,500 crore; Rs 1,890 crore is held against three large SMA accounts.

qa_highlights.question: Is there stress building from the geopolitical situation or from the ECLGS 5.0 scheme?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 slippages of Rs 2,771 crore were in line with Mar-25 (Rs 2,702 crore), and no stress is visible as of now. The ECL-5 scheme is expected to add Rs 18,000-20,000 crore of exposure against about Rs 90,000 crore of affected portfolio, giving some boost to advances.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 credit guidance of 11-12% lower than FY26 growth of 15%+?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is conservative, based on GDP growth projection of 6.9% and past guidance practice, and expects to exceed it again.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the change in agri gold loan growth and current account?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said agri gold grew about 15% and total gold loans 33-34%; the agri slowdown followed RBI directions on restricted customers. Current account decline was attributed to four large-ticket accounts.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for SMA and credit cost on a run-rate basis after ECL?
qa_highlights.answer: SMA 0 Rs 10,961 crore, SMA 1 Rs 13,035 crore, SMA 2 Rs 9,732 crore (total Rs 33,728 crore). Management expects slippages and credit cost to stay in the current range, citing lower SMA balances.

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank raise capital for ECL?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it may raise capital if needed; the board has not yet approved it, and details would be shared in a couple of months.

qa_highlights.question: Segment-wise slippages in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: MSME Rs 1,333 crore, agriculture Rs 886 crore, retail Rs 431 crore, corporate Rs 80 crore, gold loans Rs 41 crore.

risks_watch: ECL transition: about Rs 10,000 crore total impact (Rs 2,500 crore stage 2 floor move, Rs 2,500-5,000 crore PD-related, Rs 2,500 crore non-fund), system-level implementation in September 2026; stage-wise absolute provisions not yet disclosed and CRAR impact about 1% if absorbed upfront.
Capital raise: management said it may raise capital if needed; board approval pending, details promised within a couple of months.

Asset quality: Q4 slippages Rs 2,771 crore with MSME Rs 1,333 crore; management says no stress visible yet, but ECLGS 5.0 could add Rs 18,000-20,000 crore exposure and geopolitical stress is a watch item.
Margin: NIM guided at 2.5-2.6% after 9 bps QoQ gain; deposit repricing and the December repo cut (about 50% of advances repo-linked) could pressure yields if deposit costs rise.

Earnings quality: Q4 included Rs 800 crore MTM losses (bond yields 6.59% to 7.05%); Q1 FY27 already has Rs 300 crore big-ticket TWO recovery, but quarterly TWO recovery has been volatile (Rs 1,646 crore in Q4 vs Rs 2,051 crore in Q3).

Gold loans and fraud: gold book about 20% of advances, growing 33-34%; management did not disclose a Q4 fraud amount, and a fraud-related media report was raised on the call. Agri gold growth slower at about 15% under RBI restrictions; current account declined on four large accounts.

summary.management_tone: Management was confident and assertive on growth, asset quality and ability to absorb ECL, repeatedly calling SMA, slippage and NIM levels industry-best. It was evasive on specifics: it declined to name the four current-account accounts, gave no stage-wise provision numbers pending system implementation, and said the capital raise decision awaited board approval.

growth.why: FY27 advances growth guided at 11-12% (midpoint 11.5%) and management expects to beat it after FY26 delivered 15.30% against 10-11% guidance; backing is partial, citing strong RAM/retail/gold demand and repricing, with no specific capacity or order book numbers.
